subject: mathematics
question_text: If the vectors λi − 3j + 5k and 2λi − λj − k are perpendicular to each other, then find λ.

mark_split.label: Set the dot product to zero

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.89 — VSAQ chapter 17 Product of Vectors, answer 119.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would find lambda here — and say how many answers you expect.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set the dot product to zero
steps.margin_note: First mark. The condition is still a·b = 0, but λ appears in BOTH vectors — so the equation will be quadratic, not linear.
steps.memory_tip: Same condition, but λ appears in BOTH vectors — so the equation comes out quadratic, not linear.
lines: Let a = λi − 3j + 5k, b = 2λi − λj − k

recall.must_convey: That a·b = 0 is written down, and that λ appears in both vectors so the equation is quadratic.
accept: set the dot product to zero, lambda is in both vectors so it will be quadratic
a dot b equals zero gives an equation with lambda squared
write the perpendicular condition, it produces a quadratic
dot product zero, rendu vectors lo lambda undi kabatti quadratic vasthundi
the condition gives a quadratic in lambda

steps.why: λ multiplying λ is what makes this quadratic. Noticing that up front is what tells you to expect two answers rather than one.
common_mistakes: Assuming there will be a single answer.
Dropping the minus signs when multiplying.

steps.label: Solve the quadratic
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Factorise rather than reaching for the formula. BOTH roots are valid answers — the question did not exclude either.
steps.memory_tip: Factorise rather than using the formula. BOTH roots are valid; nothing excludes either.

recall.must_convey: That the quadratic 2λ² + 3λ − 5 = 0 factorises to give TWO answers, λ = 1 and λ = −5/2.
accept: factorise to lambda minus one into two lambda plus five so lambda is one or minus five by two
there are two answers, one and minus five over two
solving the quadratic gives lambda equals one or minus five halves
rendu answers vasthai, one and minus five by two
both roots are valid so lambda is one or minus two point five

steps.why: A quadratic has two roots and nothing in the question rules either out, so both must be reported. Giving only one is giving half the answer.
common_mistakes: Discarding the negative root for no reason.

insider_note: λ appears in BOTH vectors, so the dot product is a quadratic and not a linear equation. Two answers follow, 1 and −5/2, and giving only the whole one loses half the marks.
